this_experiment_findings.title: Stated gate 'at least one assigned user opted in' is not what the code implements
this_experiment_findings.problem: The PR states a self-driving inbox PR is stamphog-reviewed when 'at least one of the assigned users has stamphog_review_inbox_prs enabled' (and Case 1 step 3 says 'whether any assigned reviewer opted in'). The code resolves exactly one acting reviewer via _resolve_assigned_reviewer — the task creator if they are among the resolved reviewers, otherwise the first resolved reviewer — and checks only that one user's row. If the acting reviewer has the toggle off but a later reviewer in the assigned set has it on, no stamphog review runs. The same single-acting-reviewer rule is a documented maintainer decision for the review_inbox_prs gate, so the code is likely intentional and the PR copy is the loose part, but as written the PR description promises behavior the code does not deliver.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: Align the two. If single-acting-reviewer gating is intended, tighten the PR description to say the acting reviewer's toggle gates the review (creator-if-assigned, else first assigned reviewer). If the any-assigned-user semantics is actually wanted, resolve_all candidates and dispatch per opted-in reviewer — but note that would also need a dedupe story, since two opted-in reviewers on one PR would each queue a stamphog review of the same PR.
this_experiment_findings.match_reason: Same claim and anchor (receivers.py:111-126): the gate checks one canonical acting reviewer's toggle, so an opted-in non-canonical assigned reviewer is ignored, contradicting the PR's 'any assigned reviewer opted in' description.

The stamphog webhook re-check at lines 151-156 (resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer) uses the same single-reviewer rule. this_experiment_findings.title: PR contract says "at least one assigned user opted in", but the code gates on the single acting reviewer's toggle only
this_experiment_findings.problem: The PR description states a Stamphog review runs when "at least one of the assigned users has stamphog_review_inbox_prs enabled" (Case 1 step 3: "checks whether any assigned reviewer opted in"). The implementation does something narrower: _resolve_assigned_reviewer picks exactly one acting reviewer (the task creator if they are in the assigned set, otherwise the first resolved reviewer), and resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer then checks only that one user's toggle. When the acting reviewer's toggle is off but another assigned reviewer has it on, no Stamphog review runs. The same mismatch applies to the review_inbox_prs leg at lines 114-121. Either the description overstates the behavior, or the code under-implements it; a reader of the PR (and of the Inbox "For you" semantics the resolution mirrors) cannot tell which one is intended.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: Reconcile the two. If the single-acting-reviewer model is the intended design (the docstrings on _resolve_assigned_reviewer and ReviewUserSettings read that way), correct the PR description's "at least one of the assigned users" wording so the documented contract matches the code. If "any assigned reviewer" is truly wanted, the resolver would need to check the toggle across all resolved reviewers instead of only the acting one, and the ReviewHog options would still need a single owner.
this_experiment_findings.match_reason: Same claim and anchor (receivers.py:144-160): the gate checks only the single canonical acting reviewer's toggle, contradicting the PR's 'at least one assigned user opted in' contract.

The code in the worktree gates on exactly one user: /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215/products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:206 `acting = next((user for user in resolved if user.id == task_created_by_id), resolved[0])` returns a single id; `handle_task_run_saved` at receivers.py:111-114 loads `ReviewUserSettings.load(instance.team_id, acting_user_id)` for that one user and checks `review_inbox_prs` (114) and `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` (125); `resolve_stamphog_acting_reviewer` at receivers.py:151-156 does the same single-user check for the webhook leg, which products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:205-207 treats as `opted_out=True` when None. The refutation fails on the mismatch itself; what it does establish is that the code is coherent, documented, and tested as intended, so the only actionable fix is the PR description wording. Because nothing incorrect ships in code (the cited receivers.py lines behave as their docstrings say), this is a documentation-only inaccuracy in the PR body rather than a should_fix defect; the separate user-facing confusion (a non-canonical assignee toggling on and seeing nothing) is inherent in the chosen design and is covered by other findings about UI copy, not by this one.

Existing tests pin the single-reviewer semantic as intended, i.e. the opposite of "any assigned": products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py:229-239 `test_opted_out_canonical_reviewer_blocks_the_review` asserts no review runs when the canonical reviewer is off and a second assigned reviewer (alice) is on; test_inbox_trigger.py:256-268 `test_non_assigned_requester_follows_the_canonical_reviewer` asserts the same for an opted-in non-assigned creator; test_inbox_trigger.py:324-379 checks the stamphog toggle through that same single acting reviewer. fresh_votes.refutation: Attempted refutation: the mismatch could be dismissed if the PR body's "at least one assigned user" were merely loose prose for the same behavior, or if the code actually iterated all assignees. What the refutation does establish is that the defect is confined to the PR body: the code, its tests, AGENTS.md, README, model docstring, serializer help_text and UI copy are all mutually consistent on "the acting reviewer's toggle". No code change is warranted and nothing incorrect ships in the repository, so this is a real but minor documentation correction (fix the PR description wording), not a should_fix defect.

this_experiment_findings.title: Stamphog checks only one assigned reviewer
this_experiment_findings.problem: The feature must run when any assigned reviewer enables the Stamphog toggle. This code first selects one acting reviewer. It then checks only that user's setting. A primary reviewer with the toggle off blocks the review, even when another assigned reviewer opted in. The webhook resolver repeats this behavior, so later commits also skip review.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: Resolve all assigned reviewers for the Stamphog path. Prefer the task creator when that user is assigned and opted in. Otherwise, select the first assigned reviewer with `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` enabled. Use the same selection logic for the initial dispatch and webhook re-reviews. Add a regression test with two assignees where only the second assignee opted in.
this_experiment_findings.match_reason: Claims the gate resolves one canonical acting reviewer and checks only that user's stamphog toggle, so an opted-in non-canonical assignee is ignored on both legs, at receivers.py:111-126/144-155, matching cluster 57's claim and anchors exactly.

this_experiment_findings.title: Only one assigned reviewer can enable Stamphog
this_experiment_findings.problem: The PR requires a review when at least one assigned user enables the toggle. This code selects one acting reviewer before it checks the toggle. It skips the review when that user opts out, even if another assigned reviewer opts in. The webhook resolver repeats the same behavior, so later commits also skip review.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: Resolve all assigned reviewers and select an opted-in user. Preserve the current creator-first ordering among users who enabled `stamphog_review_inbox_prs`. Use the same selection for the initial receiver and the webhook resolver. Add a case where the first reviewer opts out and a second reviewer opts in.
this_experiment_findings.match_reason: Claims the gate consults a single canonical acting reviewer's toggle so an opted-in secondary assigned reviewer is ignored, at receivers.py:111-126 and the webhook resolver at 150-156, matching cluster 57's claim and anchors.

fresh_votes.refutation: The finding's premise ("The PR requires a review when at least one assigned user enables the toggle") is asserted, not sourced; nothing in the worktree states that requirement. The code, module and function docstrings, DECISIONS.md, and a dedicated regression test all state the opposite: one canonical acting reviewer whose toggle gates the review, and a secondary reviewer's opt-in must not hijack it.
